scenarios.name: native_commit_missing_block_and_vote_immutability
checks: retransmitting an authentic vote leaves two distinct prevotes and no lock
three actual prevotes update both native lock and valid-block fields before a non-nil precommit
the native executor validates, persists, and applies a normal three-signature commit
the same emitted precommit bytes and Ed25519 verification survive local height advancement
three real precommits enter Commit but do not invent missing block data
delivery of the corresponding Merkle-checked block parts completes the same normal commit at a catching-up node

scenarios.name: native_mixed_quorum_timeout_guards
checks: a scheduled proposal timeout without block data emits a native nil prevote
two distinct prevotes do not schedule prevote-wait; a mixed three-vote quorum does, and its timeout signs nil
two distinct precommits do not schedule round advancement; three nil precommits schedule a timeout whose firing advances exactly one round

scenarios.name: native_lock_persistence_and_locked_prevote
checks: legal mixed-precommit timeout advances the round while preserving native lock and valid-block state
the unchanged native prevote rule votes for its old lock after receiving a different valid proposal from the actual next proposer
this conformance scenario produces no commit and no agreement violation

scenarios.name: native_valid_block_proposal_reuse
checks: the actual round-1 proposer with validBlock@0 reuses that block and publishes POLRound=0
the locally retained real PoLC makes the reused proposal complete and yields a matching native prevote

limits: Unmodified-source normal-operation conformance, not a fault-injection witness or native disagreement experiment.
In-process State message/timeout dispatch and official local application fixture; no reactor, sockets, persistent validator signer, or WAL receive loop.
Actual Ed25519 with deterministic test keys via upstream MockPV; no production key material.
A fixed deterministic event order; native wall-clock timestamps/signatures are retained and need not be byte-identical across reruns.
Four finite scenarios validate exercised guards; they are neither exhaustive verification nor a refinement proof.
